newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese May net foreign stock buying hits record.
newsitem.headline: Japanese May net foreign stock buying hits record.

text.p: Japanese net foreign stock buying in May hit a record high of 607.0 billion yen, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told reporters on Wednesday.

One of the factors for the record high purchases was the that U.S. economic indicators for May such as the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) and employment data showed strong growth in the U.S. economy, the official said.
The indicators also reduced concerns of inflation in the United States, the official said.
Another reason was comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan which markets took to indicate that the Fed would keep its interest rates steady, the official said.
The previous record for Japanese net foreign stock buying was 597.4 billion yen in April 1996.
